meta.name: OR-Benchmark-GraphRAG
meta.description: A benchmark-oriented graph of OR modeling patterns, code skeletons, typical errors, and fix hints for NL4OPT, MAMO, IndustryOR, OptiBench, and OptMathBench.
meta.mamo_easy_update: added four MAMO Easy-specific variants for short two-variable allocation, ratio/difference constraints, lower-bound positive-cost allocation, and objective-unit sanity checks

nodes.name: Direct formula or derived KPI description
nodes.text: The prompt asks for a computed value, total, capacity, availability, ratio, or KPI from stated constants and formulas, without asking the solver to choose an optimal decision.

nodes.name: Direct formula or derived KPI model
nodes.text: Do not invent decision variables, artificial objectives, or capacity constraints. Extract the stated quantities and compute the requested value directly with arithmetic, recurrences, or table aggregation.

nodes.name: Direct formula or derived KPI code skeleton
nodes.snippet: result = sum(value[t] * rate[t] for t in periods); print('result:', result)

nodes.name: InventedOptimization
nodes.text: A deterministic calculation is incorrectly turned into an optimization problem with invented decision variables or objectives.

nodes.name: InventedOptimization fix
nodes.text: If the question only asks for a computed value and gives no objective to optimize, solve it as direct arithmetic and print the computed value.

nodes.name: WrongAggregationWindow
nodes.text: The computation includes the wrong time periods or omits a stated period boundary.

nodes.name: WrongAggregationWindow fix
nodes.text: Track the exact horizon words such as before, by the start of, after, over, per year, and include only the relevant periods.

nodes.name: UnitOrRateMismatch
nodes.text: Rates, units, or conversion factors are multiplied by the wrong quantity.

nodes.name: UnitOrRateMismatch fix
nodes.text: Write the formula with units first, then substitute numbers. Do not mix production units, people, money, and capacity without the stated conversion rate.

nodes.name: Multi-activity resource allocation description
nodes.text: Choose activity levels under several resource limits, usually maximizing profit/value or minimizing total cost.

nodes.name: Multi-activity resource allocation model
nodes.text: Create one variable per activity. Add one linear constraint per resource or requirement. Use <= for capacities and >= for minimum requirements. Objective is the requested total profit, cost, time, or value.

nodes.name: Multi-activity resource allocation code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVars(activities, lb=0); model.addConstrs(quicksum(a[r,i]*x[i] for i in activities) <= cap[r] for r in resources); model.setObjective(quicksum(value[i]*x[i] for i in activities), GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: ObjectiveDirection
nodes.text: The model optimizes the opposite direction because profit/value and cost/time are confused.

nodes.name: ObjectiveDirection fix
nodes.text: Use GRB.MAXIMIZE for profit, value, revenue, coverage; use GRB.MINIMIZE for cost, time, penalty, resource use.

nodes.name: MissingResource
nodes.text: A stated resource limit is omitted or merged into an unrelated constraint.

nodes.name: MissingResource fix
nodes.text: Enumerate every resource sentence and create one constraint for each distinct resource.

nodes.name: CoefficientMismatch
nodes.text: Coefficients are assigned to the wrong activity or resource.

nodes.name: CoefficientMismatch fix
nodes.text: Build a small activity-by-resource table before writing constraints, then map each row and column consistently.

nodes.name: Two-variable textbook LP description
nodes.text: A compact LP with two activities or products, individual bounds, and a shared resource constraint.

nodes.name: Two-variable textbook LP model
nodes.text: Use x and y as activity quantities. Add individual bounds x <= ux, y <= uy, lower bounds if stated, and shared constraints like a*x + b*y <= capacity.

nodes.name: Two-variable textbook LP code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVar(lb=0); y=model.addVar(lb=0); model.addConstr(x <= ux); model.addConstr(y <= uy); model.addConstr(a*x+b*y <= cap); model.setObjective(px*x+py*y, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: MissingSharedConstraint
nodes.text: Only individual bounds are modeled while the combined/shared capacity is dropped.

nodes.name: MissingSharedConstraint fix
nodes.text: Add aggregate constraints separately from individual bounds.

nodes.name: UnnecessaryEquality
nodes.text: Total capacity is forced as equality even when the statement only gives an upper bound.

nodes.name: UnnecessaryEquality fix
nodes.text: Use <= unless the text says exactly or all capacity must be used.

nodes.name: DomainMistake
nodes.text: Count variables are continuous or divisible quantities are forced integer.

nodes.name: DomainMistake fix
nodes.text: Use integer for countable objects; use continuous for money, mass, length, time, or acreage unless stated otherwise.

nodes.name: Minimum-cost requirement fulfillment description
nodes.text: Select quantities to satisfy demand, nutrition, service, or technical requirements at minimum cost or resource use.

nodes.name: Minimum-cost requirement fulfillment model
nodes.text: The objective minimizes total cost. Requirement constraints use >=. Capacity, budget, or upper-limit constraints use <=.

nodes.name: Minimum-cost requirement fulfillment code skeleton
nodes.snippet: model.setObjective(quicksum(cost[i]*x[i] for i in items), GRB.MINIMIZE); model.addConstrs(quicksum(req[k,i]*x[i] for i in items) >= demand[k] for k in requirements)

nodes.name: InequalityDirection
nodes.text: Minimum requirements are written as <=, making the solution under-satisfy demand.

nodes.name: InequalityDirection fix
nodes.text: Translate at least, minimum, require, need, demand into >=.

nodes.name: ObjectiveMetric
nodes.text: The objective uses a feasible quantity rather than the requested minimized metric.

nodes.name: ObjectiveMetric fix
nodes.text: Read the final question and minimize exactly the requested cost, time, penalty, or resource use.

nodes.name: OverconstrainedTotal
nodes.text: A total amount is fixed even though the problem only requires at least that amount.

nodes.name: OverconstrainedTotal fix
nodes.text: Use == only for exact totals; otherwise use >= or <= as stated.

nodes.name: Ratio and percentage constraints description
nodes.text: Natural language states proportions such as at least 30 percent of total, at most twice another quantity, or a minimum share.

nodes.name: Ratio and percentage constraints model
nodes.text: For x at least p percent of total, write x >= p*(x+y+...). For x at most k times y, write x <= k*y. Avoid division by variables.

nodes.name: Ratio and percentage constraints code skeleton
nodes.snippet: model.addConstr(x >= p * quicksum(vars)); model.addConstr(x <= k*y)

nodes.name: WrongDenominator
nodes.text: A percentage of total is modeled as a percentage of only one other variable.

nodes.name: WrongDenominator fix
nodes.text: Identify the denominator. If the text says total, use the sum of all relevant variables.

nodes.name: RatioDirection
nodes.text: At least k times is reversed into <= or at most k times is reversed into >=.

nodes.name: RatioDirection fix
nodes.text: For A at least k times B, write A >= k*B. For A at most k times B, write A <= k*B.

nodes.name: NonlinearDivision
nodes.text: The model divides by a decision variable and becomes nonlinear unnecessarily.

nodes.name: NonlinearDivision fix
nodes.text: Cross multiply constants and keep the expression linear.

nodes.name: Advertising channel allocation description
nodes.text: Allocate budget or ad counts across channels with spend limits, reach, frequency, or minimum campaign requirements.

nodes.name: Advertising channel allocation model
nodes.text: Variables represent spend or ad counts by channel. Budget constraints use cost*quantity <= budget. Reach constraints use exposure coefficients.

nodes.name: Advertising channel allocation code skeleton
nodes.snippet: ads=model.addVars(channels, lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER); model.addConstr(quicksum(cost[c]*ads[c] for c in channels) <= budget); model.setObjective(quicksum(reach[c]*ads[c] for c in channels), GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: SpendVsCount
nodes.text: Ad counts and spending variables are mixed without multiplying by cost per ad.

nodes.name: SpendVsCount fix
nodes.text: If the variable is an ad count, multiply it by unit cost in the budget constraint.

nodes.name: WrongObjective
nodes.text: The objective maximizes budget spent instead of reach, profit, or effect.

nodes.name: WrongObjective fix
nodes.text: Use the metric named in the question as the objective.

nodes.name: IntegerCounts
nodes.text: Ad slots or campaigns are allowed to be fractional.

nodes.name: IntegerCounts fix
nodes.text: Use integer variables for counts of ads, slots, posts, or campaigns.

nodes.name: Single-period production capacity description
nodes.text: Decide production quantities for products under labor, machine, material, or component capacity constraints.

nodes.name: Single-period production capacity model
nodes.text: Variables are product quantities. Objective maximizes profit or minimizes production cost. Add one constraint per resource capacity and product-specific bounds.

nodes.name: Single-period production capacity code skeleton
nodes.snippet: q=model.addVars(products, lb=0); model.addConstrs(quicksum(use[r,p]*q[p] for p in products) <= cap[r] for r in resources); model.setObjective(quicksum(profit[p]*q[p] for p in products), GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: CapacityOmission
nodes.text: A labor, machine, or material capacity is not modeled.

nodes.name: CapacityOmission fix
nodes.text: Create a resource checklist and add one constraint for each resource.

nodes.name: ProfitDefinition
nodes.text: Revenue is used as profit while variable costs should be subtracted.

nodes.name: ProfitDefinition fix
nodes.text: When costs and selling prices are both given, use unit profit = price minus cost unless the problem directly gives profit.

nodes.name: IntegerProduction
nodes.text: Discrete units are fractional when products are indivisible.

nodes.name: IntegerProduction fix
nodes.text: Use integer variables for indivisible products if the benchmark expects counts.

nodes.name: Multi-period production, inventory, and workforce description
nodes.text: Plan production, outsourcing, inventory, hiring, or firing across periods while satisfying period demand.

nodes.name: Multi-period production, inventory, and workforce model
nodes.text: Index variables by period. Inventory balance is inventory[t-1] + production[t] + outsourcing[t] - demand[t] = inventory[t]. Workforce balance is workforce[t] = workforce[t-1] + hire[t] - fire[t].

nodes.name: Multi-period production, inventory, and workforce code skeleton
nodes.snippet: model.addConstrs(inv[t-1]+prod[t]+outs[t]-demand[t] == inv[t] for t in periods); model.addConstrs(work[t] == work[t-1]+hire[t]-fire[t] for t in periods)

nodes.name: BalanceEquation
nodes.text: Inventory or workforce balance ignores the previous period state.

nodes.name: BalanceEquation fix
nodes.text: Write recursive balance equations with t-1 state, inflow, outflow, and t state.

nodes.name: InitialState
nodes.text: Initial inventory or workforce is not included in period 1.

nodes.name: InitialState fix
nodes.text: Use the given initial condition for the first period balance.

nodes.name: PeriodIndex
nodes.text: A single aggregate demand constraint replaces period-specific constraints.

nodes.name: PeriodIndex fix
nodes.text: Keep demand, capacity, and balance constraints indexed by period.

nodes.name: Shift coverage scheduling description
nodes.text: Choose shift starts or staff levels so each time interval is covered by enough workers at minimum cost.

nodes.name: Shift coverage scheduling model
nodes.text: Variables are workers starting each shift. For each time interval, sum variables whose shifts cover it and require coverage >= demand.

nodes.name: Shift coverage scheduling code skeleton
nodes.snippet: start=model.addVars(shifts, lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER); model.addConstrs(quicksum(cover[s,t]*start[s] for s in shifts) >= demand[t] for t in times)

nodes.name: CoverageDirection
nodes.text: Coverage is constrained with <= demand, allowing understaffing.

nodes.name: CoverageDirection fix
nodes.text: Use provided staff >= required staff for each interval.

nodes.name: ShiftCoverageMap
nodes.text: A shift is counted in the wrong time interval.

nodes.name: ShiftCoverageMap fix
nodes.text: Build a binary cover[s,t] table before coding constraints.

nodes.name: FractionalWorkers
nodes.text: The solution uses fractional workers or shifts.

nodes.name: FractionalWorkers fix
nodes.text: Use integer variables for staff counts and shift starts.

nodes.name: Diet, feed, or mixture blending description
nodes.text: Mix ingredients or foods to satisfy nutrient, chemical, or quality bounds at minimum cost.

nodes.name: Diet, feed, or mixture blending model
nodes.text: Variables are ingredient amounts. Nutrient minimums use >=. Toxicity, fat, impurity, or maximum composition use <=. Include a total amount constraint if specified.

nodes.name: Diet, feed, or mixture blending code skeleton
nodes.snippet: amt=model.addVars(items, lb=0); model.addConstrs(quicksum(nutr[k,i]*amt[i] for i in items) >= min_req[k] for k in nutrients); model.setObjective(quicksum(cost[i]*amt[i] for i in items), GRB.MINIMIZE)

nodes.name: NutrientDirection
nodes.text: Minimum nutrition constraints are written as upper bounds.

nodes.name: NutrientDirection fix
nodes.text: Use >= for minimum nutrition or quality requirements.

nodes.name: CompositionTotal
nodes.text: Percentage quality constraints are applied to one ingredient instead of the whole mixture.

nodes.name: CompositionTotal fix
nodes.text: Use percentage times total mixture amount.

nodes.name: MissingTotalAmount
nodes.text: The required total amount of blend or meal is omitted.

nodes.name: MissingTotalAmount fix
nodes.text: If a target total amount is stated, add sum ingredients == or >= that amount.

nodes.name: Transportation supply-demand model description
nodes.text: Ship goods from origins to destinations with origin supply and destination demand constraints, minimizing shipping cost.

nodes.name: Transportation supply-demand model model
nodes.text: Variables x[i,j] are shipment amounts. Origin constraints sum_j x[i,j] <= supply[i]. Destination constraints sum_i x[i,j] >= demand[j] or == demand[j] if exact.

nodes.name: Transportation supply-demand model code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVars(origins,dests,lb=0); model.addConstrs(x.sum(i,'*') <= supply[i] for i in origins); model.addConstrs(x.sum('*',j) >= demand[j] for j in dests)

nodes.name: SupplyDemandDirection
nodes.text: Supply and demand inequalities are reversed.

nodes.name: SupplyDemandDirection fix
nodes.text: Supply is usually an upper bound at origins; demand is a lower or exact requirement at destinations.

nodes.name: IndexSummation
nodes.text: The supply constraint sums origins instead of destinations or vice versa.

nodes.name: IndexSummation fix
nodes.text: For supply fix origin and sum destinations; for demand fix destination and sum origins.

nodes.name: UseAllSupply
nodes.text: All supply is forced to ship even when unused supply is allowed.

nodes.name: UseAllSupply fix
nodes.text: Use <= for supply unless the problem says all supply must be shipped.

nodes.name: Network flow and shortest path description
nodes.text: Choose flows or paths through a node-arc network with conservation, capacity, cost, or shortest-path constraints.

nodes.name: Network flow and shortest path model
nodes.text: Use arc variables. Flow conservation: outflow - inflow equals supply at source, -demand at sink, and 0 at intermediate nodes. For shortest path use binary arc variables and one-unit flow.

nodes.name: Network flow and shortest path code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVars(arcs, lb=0); model.addConstrs(quicksum(x[i,j] for j in out[n]) - quicksum(x[i,n] for i in inn[n]) == b[n] for n in nodes)

nodes.name: ConservationSign
nodes.text: Flow conservation signs are inconsistent across nodes.

nodes.name: ConservationSign fix
nodes.text: Pick one convention, such as outflow minus inflow equals node supply, and use it everywhere.

nodes.name: CapacityMissing
nodes.text: Arc capacities or bandwidth limits are ignored.

nodes.name: CapacityMissing fix
nodes.text: Add x[i,j] <= capacity[i,j] for each capacitated arc.

nodes.name: PathContinuity
nodes.text: Selected arcs do not form a continuous path.

nodes.name: PathContinuity fix
nodes.text: Use flow conservation or predecessor/successor constraints to enforce continuity.

nodes.name: TSP, VRP, and route selection description
nodes.text: Build routes visiting customers or cities while minimizing travel cost and satisfying visit, depot, capacity, or time-window constraints.

nodes.name: TSP, VRP, and route selection model
nodes.text: Binary x[i,j] indicates travel from i to j. Add exactly-one incoming and outgoing constraints for visited nodes. Add subtour elimination or flow/order variables. VRP adds vehicle capacity and depot constraints.

nodes.name: TSP, VRP, and route selection code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVars(nodes,nodes,vtype=GRB.BINARY); model.addConstrs(quicksum(x[i,j] for j in nodes if j!=i)==1 for i in customers); model.addConstrs(quicksum(x[i,j] for i in nodes if i!=j)==1 for j in customers)

nodes.name: Subtour
nodes.text: The route constraints allow multiple disconnected cycles.

nodes.name: Subtour fix
nodes.text: Add subtour elimination, MTZ/order variables, or a single-commodity flow formulation.

nodes.name: DegreeConstraint
nodes.text: A customer can be entered or left more than once.

nodes.name: DegreeConstraint fix
nodes.text: Use exactly-one incoming and exactly-one outgoing constraints for each required customer.

nodes.name: DepotCapacity
nodes.text: Vehicle capacity or depot start/end constraints are missing.

nodes.name: DepotCapacity fix
nodes.text: For VRP, link each route to a vehicle, depot, and load capacity.

nodes.name: Jobshop or flowshop makespan description
nodes.text: Schedule operations on machines with processing times, precedence within jobs, and no-overlap constraints on shared machines.

nodes.name: Jobshop or flowshop makespan model
nodes.text: Start time variables for operations. Completion = start + processing. Precedence constraints enforce job order. No-overlap constraints use binary disjunctions for operations sharing a machine. Minimize makespan.

nodes.name: Jobshop or flowshop makespan code skeleton
nodes.snippet: start=model.addVars(ops, lb=0); Cmax=model.addVar(lb=0); model.addConstrs(start[next[o]] >= start[o]+p[o] for o in precedence); model.setObjective(Cmax, GRB.MINIMIZE)

nodes.name: PrecedenceMissing
nodes.text: Operations within the same job are not ordered.

nodes.name: PrecedenceMissing fix
nodes.text: Add start[next] >= start[current] + processing[current] for every job precedence arc.

nodes.name: OverlapMissing
nodes.text: Two operations use the same machine at the same time.

nodes.name: OverlapMissing fix
nodes.text: Add disjunctive no-overlap constraints with binary order variables for each machine conflict.

nodes.name: MakespanLink
nodes.text: Makespan is minimized but not constrained to be at least every job completion.

nodes.name: MakespanLink fix
nodes.text: Add Cmax >= completion[o] for all terminal operations or all operations as appropriate.

nodes.name: Time-window scheduling with separation penalties description
nodes.text: Schedule events such as aircraft landings within time windows, with separation times and earliness/lateness penalties.

nodes.name: Time-window scheduling with separation penalties model
nodes.text: Use continuous start/landing times, penalty deviation variables, binary order variables for pairwise separation, and objective minimizing weighted penalties.

nodes.name: Time-window scheduling with separation penalties code skeleton
nodes.snippet: t=model.addVars(items, lb=0); early=model.addVars(items, lb=0); late=model.addVars(items, lb=0); model.addConstrs(t[i]+sep[i,j] <= t[j] + M*(1-y[i,j]) for i,j in pairs)

nodes.name: PairwiseOrder
nodes.text: Separation is enforced in only one direction or not linked to ordering variables.

nodes.name: PairwiseOrder fix
nodes.text: For each pair, use binary order variables so either i before j or j before i holds.

nodes.name: PenaltyLinearization
nodes.text: Early and late penalties are computed with absolute values directly.

nodes.name: PenaltyLinearization fix
nodes.text: Use nonnegative early and late deviation variables tied to target time.

nodes.name: WindowBounds
nodes.text: Earliest and latest times are treated as soft penalties instead of hard bounds.

nodes.name: WindowBounds fix
nodes.text: Add earliest <= t[i] <= latest when the window is mandatory.

nodes.name: Task assignment and matching description
nodes.text: Assign workers, machines, jobs, or tasks using binary decisions with coverage, capacity, skill, or availability constraints.

nodes.name: Task assignment and matching model
nodes.text: Binary x[i,j]. Each task is assigned exactly once or at least once as stated. Each resource has capacity constraints. Skill restrictions force x[i,j] = 0 when infeasible.

nodes.name: Task assignment and matching code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVars(workers,tasks,vtype=GRB.BINARY); model.addConstrs(x.sum('*',j)==1 for j in tasks); model.addConstrs(x.sum(i,'*')<=cap[i] for i in workers)

nodes.name: BinaryDomain
nodes.text: Assignment decisions are continuous instead of binary.

nodes.name: BinaryDomain fix
nodes.text: Use GRB.BINARY for yes/no assignment variables.

nodes.name: CoverageCapacity
nodes.text: Only task coverage or only worker capacity is modeled.

nodes.name: CoverageCapacity fix
nodes.text: Model both sides: task demand and resource capacity.

nodes.name: FeasibilityRestriction
nodes.text: Assignments forbidden by skills or availability are still allowed.

nodes.name: FeasibilityRestriction fix
nodes.text: Set x[i,j] == 0 or omit variables for infeasible pairs.

nodes.name: Facility opening and customer assignment description
nodes.text: Decide which facilities to open and how to assign customers or demand to opened facilities.

nodes.name: Facility opening and customer assignment model
nodes.text: Binary y[j] indicates opened facility. x[i,j] is assignment or shipped demand. Link x[i,j] to y[j]. Objective includes fixed opening cost plus service or transport cost.

nodes.name: Facility opening and customer assignment code skeleton
nodes.snippet: y=model.addVars(facilities,vtype=GRB.BINARY); x=model.addVars(customers,facilities,lb=0); model.addConstrs(x[i,j] <= demand[i]*y[j] for i in customers for j in facilities)

nodes.name: OpenLink
nodes.text: Demand is assigned to a closed facility.

nodes.name: OpenLink fix
nodes.text: Add x[i,j] <= demand[i]*y[j] or binary x[i,j] <= y[j].

nodes.name: FixedCost
nodes.text: Facility opening fixed cost is omitted from the objective.

nodes.name: FixedCost fix
nodes.text: Include fixed_cost[j]*y[j] whenever fixed costs are stated.

nodes.name: CoverageMissing
nodes.text: Some customer demand can remain unserved without penalty.

nodes.name: CoverageMissing fix
nodes.text: Add demand coverage constraints for every customer or area.

nodes.name: Set cover and maximum coverage description
nodes.text: Select sets, facilities, towers, or services to cover areas or requirements under budget or cardinality limits.

nodes.name: Set cover and maximum coverage model
nodes.text: Binary y[j] selects a set/facility. Cover constraints require sum covering sets >= 1 for set cover. Maximum coverage may use covered-area variables z[i] linked to selected facilities.

nodes.name: Set cover and maximum coverage code skeleton
nodes.snippet: y=model.addVars(sets,vtype=GRB.BINARY); z=model.addVars(areas,vtype=GRB.BINARY); model.addConstrs(z[i] <= quicksum(cover[j,i]*y[j] for j in sets) for i in areas)

nodes.name: CoverageLink
nodes.text: The objective counts covered areas without linking them to selected facilities.

nodes.name: CoverageLink fix
nodes.text: Use z[i] <= sum cover[j,i]*y[j] and maximize weighted z[i].

nodes.name: BudgetVsCardinality
nodes.text: A fixed number of facilities is used when the problem gives a budget, or vice versa.

nodes.name: BudgetVsCardinality fix
nodes.text: Use the stated budget or cardinality limit exactly.

nodes.name: AtLeastOne
nodes.text: Set cover constraints use <= 1 rather than >= 1.

nodes.name: AtLeastOne fix
nodes.text: To require coverage, use sum selected covering sets >= 1.

nodes.name: Knapsack, project selection, and portfolio allocation
Knapsack, project selection, and portfolio allocation description
nodes.text: Select items/projects/assets or allocate investment under budget, risk, weight, or capacity constraints.

nodes.name: Knapsack, project selection, and portfolio allocation model
nodes.text: Use binary variables for yes/no selection and continuous variables for divisible investment amounts. Add budget/capacity constraints and maximize value or return.

nodes.name: Knapsack, project selection, and portfolio allocation code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVars(items,vtype=GRB.BINARY); model.addConstr(quicksum(weight[i]*x[i] for i in items) <= capacity); model.setObjective(quicksum(value[i]*x[i] for i in items), GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: VariableType
nodes.text: Binary selection and continuous investment are confused.

nodes.name: VariableType fix
nodes.text: Use binary for choose/not choose; use continuous for amount of money invested.

nodes.name: RiskConstraint
nodes.text: Risk is put in the objective although the problem gives it as a limit.

nodes.name: RiskConstraint fix
nodes.text: Treat explicit risk caps as constraints unless the objective asks to minimize risk.

nodes.name: BudgetEquality
nodes.text: The full budget is forced to be used when only an upper limit is stated.

nodes.name: BudgetEquality fix
nodes.text: Use <= unless all budget must be invested or spent.

nodes.name: Price-demand revenue or profit optimization description
nodes.text: Optimize price or quantity when demand changes with price, producing a quadratic revenue or profit expression.

nodes.name: Price-demand revenue or profit optimization model
nodes.text: Define a price or discount decision and a demand expression. Revenue is price*demand and may be quadratic. If decisions are discrete multiples, use integer variables.

nodes.name: Price-demand revenue or profit optimization code skeleton
nodes.snippet: k=model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER); price=base_price-step*k; demand=base_demand+delta*k; model.setObjective(price*demand-fixed_cost, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: DiscreteStep
nodes.text: A price discount that must be a multiple is modeled as continuous.

nodes.name: DiscreteStep fix
nodes.text: Use an integer step variable for discrete price changes.

nodes.name: ProfitVsRevenue
nodes.text: Fixed or variable costs are ignored when the question asks for profit.

nodes.name: ProfitVsRevenue fix
nodes.text: Profit equals revenue minus stated costs.

nodes.name: LinearizationUnneeded
nodes.text: The quadratic objective is incorrectly linearized or approximated.

nodes.name: LinearizationUnneeded fix
nodes.text: Gurobi can handle quadratic objectives; keep exact expression when convexity/MIQP is acceptable.

nodes.name: Geometric area and dimension optimization description
nodes.text: Optimize dimensions such as rectangle length and width under perimeter, material, or fencing constraints.

nodes.name: Geometric area and dimension optimization model
nodes.text: Variables are dimensions. Add resource constraints such as 2*w + l <= fencing. Objective may be area l*w, a quadratic expression.

nodes.name: Geometric area and dimension optimization code skeleton
nodes.snippet: length=model.addVar(lb=0); width=model.addVar(lb=0); model.addConstr(length+2*width <= fence); model.setObjective(length*width, GRB.MAXIMIZE)

nodes.name: GeometryFormula
nodes.text: The wrong perimeter formula is used when one side is provided by a wall or house.

nodes.name: GeometryFormula fix
nodes.text: Translate the physical layout carefully, such as length + 2*width for three-sided fencing.

nodes.name: ObjectiveExpression
nodes.text: The objective optimizes perimeter instead of area.

nodes.name: ObjectiveExpression fix
nodes.text: Use area = length*width when maximizing area.

nodes.name: NonlinearSupport
nodes.text: The solver code treats the nonlinear area objective as invalid.

nodes.name: NonlinearSupport fix
nodes.text: Use Gurobi quadratic objective support for products of two variables where appropriate.

nodes.name: Quadratic objective with auxiliary variables description
nodes.text: Optimization problems include quadratic costs, deviations, norms, or auxiliary variables for convex modeling.

nodes.name: Quadratic objective with auxiliary variables model
nodes.text: Represent squared deviations directly in a quadratic objective or introduce auxiliary variables for piecewise/absolute terms. Link all auxiliary variables to primary decisions.

nodes.name: Quadratic objective with auxiliary variables code skeleton
nodes.snippet: dev=model.addVars(items, lb=-GRB.INFINITY); model.addConstrs(dev[i] == expr[i]-target[i] for i in items); model.setObjective(quicksum(w[i]*dev[i]*dev[i] for i in items), GRB.MINIMIZE)

nodes.name: AuxiliaryUnlinked
nodes.text: Auxiliary variables appear in the objective but are not linked to primary variables.

nodes.name: AuxiliaryUnlinked fix
nodes.text: Add equality constraints defining each auxiliary variable.

nodes.name: AbsoluteValue
nodes.text: Absolute values are used directly in linear code without modeling.

nodes.name: AbsoluteValue fix
nodes.text: Use nonnegative positive and negative deviation variables or supported general constraints.

nodes.name: SenseMismatch
nodes.text: Penalty expressions are maximized instead of minimized.

nodes.name: SenseMismatch fix
nodes.text: Deviation, penalty, and norm objectives are normally minimized.

nodes.name: Integer, binary, and logical constraints description
nodes.text: Problems contain count decisions, if-then logic, either-or choices, or activation constraints.

nodes.name: Integer, binary, and logical constraints model
nodes.text: Use integer variables for counts and binary variables for yes/no choices. Link conditional continuous quantities with big-M or indicator constraints.

nodes.name: Integer, binary, and logical constraints code skeleton
nodes.snippet: y=model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY); q=model.addVar(lb=0); model.addConstr(q <= M*y); model.addGenConstrIndicator(y, True, expr <= rhs)

nodes.name: SelfEqualityIntegrality
nodes.text: Integrality is represented by meaningless constraints such as x == x.

nodes.name: SelfEqualityIntegrality fix
nodes.text: Set vtype=GRB.INTEGER or GRB.BINARY on the variable.

nodes.name: BigMTooSmall
nodes.text: The big-M value cuts off feasible solutions.

nodes.name: BigMTooSmall fix
nodes.text: Choose M from a valid upper bound or use indicator constraints when possible.

nodes.name: LogicalDirection
nodes.text: Only one direction of an if-then relation is modeled when equivalence is required.

nodes.name: LogicalDirection fix
nodes.text: For if and only if, model both implications.

nodes.name: Table and matrix data parsing description
nodes.text: Problems provide costs, capacities, distances, times, or compatibility data in tables or matrices inside the prompt.

nodes.name: Table and matrix data parsing model
nodes.text: Extract data into dictionaries or lists with stable indices. Ensure rows and columns match the entities named in the question.

nodes.name: Table and matrix data parsing code skeleton
nodes.snippet: cost={(i,j): table[i][j] for i in I for j in J}; x=model.addVars(I,J,lb=0); model.setObjective(quicksum(cost[i,j]*x[i,j] for i in I for j in J), GRB.MINIMIZE)

nodes.name: RowColumnSwap
nodes.text: Rows and columns of a table are swapped in constraints or objective.

nodes.name: RowColumnSwap fix
nodes.text: Name row and column index sets explicitly and map each coefficient once.

nodes.name: MissingZeroArc
nodes.text: Zero or missing entries are treated as available arcs when they mean no direct connection.

nodes.name: MissingZeroArc fix
nodes.text: If zero means no connection, exclude that arc or set its variable to zero.

nodes.name: TranscriptionError
nodes.text: Large prompt tables are copied incorrectly into code.

nodes.name: TranscriptionError fix
nodes.text: Use compact dictionaries/lists and verify dimensions before solving.

nodes.name: Objective extraction and solver status description
nodes.text: Generated solver code must return the requested objective value and handle infeasible or no-solution cases consistently.

nodes.name: Objective extraction and solver status model
nodes.text: After optimize, check status. Return model.ObjVal for optimal/feasible optimum. Normalize infeasible and no-best-solution labels consistently.

nodes.name: Objective extraction and solver status code skeleton
nodes.snippet: model.optimize(); print(model.ObjVal if model.status == GRB.OPTIMAL else 'No Best Solution')

nodes.name: WrongOutput
nodes.text: The code prints a decision variable or status instead of the objective value.

nodes.name: WrongOutput fix
nodes.text: The benchmark usually evaluates the objective value, so print model.ObjVal.

nodes.name: NoSolutionAsZero
nodes.text: Infeasible or failed runs are returned as 0.

nodes.name: NoSolutionAsZero fix
nodes.text: Return a normalized no-solution marker unless the optimal objective is truly zero.

nodes.name: TimeLimitStatus
nodes.text: A time-limited run with incumbent is treated as exact optimum.

nodes.name: TimeLimitStatus fix
nodes.text: Use optimal status for exact evaluation or clearly record feasible-but-not-proven status.

nodes.name: Two-product resource allocation with ratio or proportion bounds
Two-product resource allocation with ratio or proportion bounds description
nodes.text: Applies to problems with two activities/products that use shared resources (e.g., land, cocoa, milk, time) and must satisfy linear capacity constraints plus a wording like 'at least k times as many A as B' or 'at most p% of the total can be type B'. Objective is usually to maximize or minimize a scalar measure (profit, time, number of units) over the two decision variables.

nodes.name: Two-product resource allocation with ratio or proportion bounds model
nodes.text:
Let x_1, x_2 be nonnegative decision variables (units of product/activity 1 and 2).
Objective: maximize or minimize Z = c_1 x_1 + c_2 x_2.
Resource constraints: for each resource r, a_{r1} x_1 + a_{r2} x_2 <= R_r (capacity) or >= R_r (requirement).
Ratio constraints:
- 'At least k times as many of 1 as 2': x_1 >= k x_2.
- 'At most k times as many of 1 as 2': x_1 <= k x_2.
Proportion constraints (type i is at most p of total):
Let p in (0,1). If type 2 is at most p of total units: x_2 <= p (x_1 + x_2). Keep it linear by rearranging: (1-p) x_2 <= p x_1, or equivalently (1-p) x_2 - p x_1 <= 0. Do not divide by decision variables. Include nonnegativity x_1 >= 0, x_2 >= 0 and integrality if units are indivisible.

nodes.name: Two-product resource allocation with ratio or proportion bounds code skeleton
nodes.snippet:
import pulp

# Parameters (example)
# Objective coefficients
c1 = 15  # time per unit of product 1
c2 = 12  # time per unit of product 2

# Resource limits
R_cocoa = 2000
R_milk = 1750

# Resource usage per unit
cocoa1, milk1 = 4, 7
cocoa2, milk2 = 6, 3

# Ratio: x1 at least 2 times x2
k = 2.0

# Build model (minimize total time)
model = pulp.LpProblem("TwoProductRatioResource", pulp.LpMinimize)

x1 = pulp.LpVariable("x1", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
x2 = pulp.LpVariable("x2", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Objective
model += c1 * x1 + c2 * x2

# Resource constraints
model += cocoa1 * x1 + cocoa2 * x2 <= R_cocoa, "CocoaCapacity"
model += milk1 * x1 + milk2 * x2 <= R_milk, "MilkCapacity"

# Ratio constraint: x1 >= k * x2
model += x1 >= k * x2, "AtLeastKTimes"

# Solve
status = model.solve(pulp.PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=False))

if pulp.LpStatus[status] == "Optimal":
    obj_val = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print("result:", obj_val)
else:
    print("result: None")

nodes.name: RatioDirection
nodes.text: Misinterpreting phrases like 'at least twice as many A as B' and writing A <= 2B instead of A >= 2B.

nodes.name: RatioDirection fix
nodes.text: Map wording carefully: 'at least k times as many A as B' means A >= k * B; 'at most k times as many A as B' means A <= k * B.

nodes.name: PercentDenominator
nodes.text: Encoding a proportion such as 'at most 35% of furnaces can be old' as O <= 0.35 * N instead of using the total N+O.

nodes.name: PercentDenominator fix
nodes.text: Identify the denominator in percentage phrases. When the text refers to the total, write constraints in terms of x_1 + x_2 (e.g., O <= 0.35 * (N + O)) and then rearrange to a linear form without dividing by variables.

nodes.name: Composition or mix with upper bound on one component's proportion
Composition or mix with upper bound on one component's proportion description
nodes.text: Applies when a mix of several components (e.g., old vs new furnaces, omega vs alpha drinks, machine types) must satisfy resource and requirement constraints, and one component is restricted to be at most a certain fraction of the total count or total amount. Decision variables are counts or quantities of each component.

nodes.name: Composition or mix with upper bound on one component's proportion model
nodes.text:
Let x_i >= 0 denote quantity or count of component i. Usual constraints include resource capacities: sum_i a_{ri} x_i <= R_r and requirement minimums: sum_i b_{qi} x_i >= Q_q. If component j must be at most proportion p of the total quantity, write
x_j <= p * (sum_i x_i).
To keep the model linear, do not divide by sum_i x_i. Instead, rearrange:
x_j - p * sum_i x_i <= 0.
For two components, x_1 and x_2, with x_2 <= p (x_1 + x_2), rearrange to (1-p) x_2 <= p x_1. If integrality is needed (units are countable), set x_i as integer decision variables.

nodes.name: Composition or mix with upper bound on one component's proportion code skeleton
nodes.snippet:
from pulp import LpProblem, LpVariable, LpMinimize, LpInteger, LpStatus, value, PULP_CBC_CMD

# Parameters (example: alpha and omega drinks)
p_alpha = 30    # protein per alpha bottle
p_omega = 20    # protein per omega bottle
c_alpha = 350   # calories per alpha bottle
c_omega = 300   # calories per omega bottle
s_alpha = 20    # sugar per alpha bottle
s_omega = 15    # sugar per omega bottle
P_min = 100     # min protein
Cal_min = 2000  # min calories
p = 0.35        # max proportion of omega bottles

model = LpProblem("CompositionProportionLimit", LpMinimize)

x_alpha = LpVariable("x_alpha", lowBound=0, cat=LpInteger)
x_omega = LpVariable("x_omega", lowBound=0, cat=LpInteger)

# Objective: minimize sugar
model += s_alpha * x_alpha + s_omega * x_omega

# Requirements
model += p_alpha * x_alpha + p_omega * x_omega >= P_min, "ProteinReq"
model += c_alpha * x_alpha + c_omega * x_omega >= Cal_min, "CalReq"

# Proportion limit: x_omega <= p * (x_alpha + x_omega)
# Rearranged to (1-p) * x_omega <= p * x_alpha
model += (1 - p) * x_omega <= p * x_alpha, "OmegaProportion"

status = model.solve(PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=False))

if LpStatus[status] == "Optimal":
    obj_val = value(model.objective)
    print("result:", obj_val)
else:
    print("result: None")

nodes.name: NonlinearDivision
nodes.text: Attempting to model a proportion like x_j / (x_1 + x_2) <= p by dividing both sides by (x_1 + x_2), creating nonlinear constraints or undefined expressions when the denominator is zero.

nodes.name: NonlinearDivision fix
nodes.text: Keep proportions linear by multiplying both sides by the total and rearranging terms, e.g., x_j <= p * (x_1 + x_2) leads to x_j - p * x_1 - p * x_2 <= 0. Never divide by decision variables.

nodes.name: FeasibilityOverlookedWithProportion
nodes.text: Adding a proportion limit together with tight capacity and requirement constraints without checking that the combined system is feasible, leading to an unintentionally infeasible model.

nodes.name: FeasibilityOverlookedWithProportion fix
nodes.text: Before coding, test simple combinations of variable values against all constraints (capacity, requirements, proportion) to confirm feasibility, or let the solver reveal infeasibility and interpret that as a property of the problem rather than a coding bug.

nodes.name: Minimize number of integer-count units subject to capacity and requirement constraints
Minimize number of integer-count units subject to capacity and requirement constraints description
nodes.text: Applies to problems where decision variables represent indivisible units (machines, furnaces, factories, jars, beakers), the objective is to minimize the total number of units, and constraints enforce minimum service/production requirements and maximum resource usages.

nodes.name: Minimize number of integer-count units subject to capacity and requirement constraints model
nodes.text:
Let x_i be nonnegative integers representing counts of units of type i.
Objective: minimize Z = sum_i x_i.
Requirement constraints: sum_i h_i x_i >= D (e.g., apartments heated, phones produced, jars filled).
Resource constraints: sum_i r_{ji} x_i <= R_j (e.g., electricity, managers, material).
Include additional bounds: x_i >= L_i (minimum units) or <= U_i (maximum units) as needed. If composition limits like 'at most p% of units are of type k' exist, combine with a proportion pattern: x_k <= p * sum_i x_i, rearranged to linear form.

nodes.name: Minimize number of integer-count units subject to capacity and requirement constraints code skeleton
nodes.snippet:
from pulp import LpProblem, LpVariable, LpMinimize, LpInteger, LpStatus, value, PULP_CBC_CMD

# Parameters (example: new and old furnaces)
h_new, h_old = 10, 15    # apartments per furnace
e_new, e_old = 200, 250  # kWh per furnace
D = 200                  # min apartments
E_max = 3500             # max electricity
p_old_max = 0.35         # max proportion old
N_min = 5                # min new furnaces

model = LpProblem("MinimizeUnits", LpMinimize)

N = LpVariable("N", lowBound=0, cat=LpInteger)  # new furnaces
O = LpVariable("O", lowBound=0, cat=LpInteger)  # old furnaces

# Objective: minimize total furnaces
model += N + O

# Requirements and capacities
model += h_new * N + h_old * O >= D, "HeatingDemand"
model += e_new * N + e_old * O <= E_max, "ElectricityLimit"

# Proportion limit: O <= p_old_max * (N + O)
model += O <= p_old_max * (N + O), "OldProportion"

# Minimum new furnaces
model += N >= N_min, "MinNew"

status = model.solve(PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=False))

if LpStatus[status] == "Optimal":
    obj_val = value(model.objective)
    print("result:", obj_val)
else:
    print("result: None")

nodes.name: CountAsContinuous
nodes.text: Modeling counts of discrete units (e.g., furnaces, factories) as continuous variables and returning fractional solutions like 12.5 furnaces.

nodes.name: CountAsContinuous fix
nodes.text: Declare decision variables for indivisible objects as integers (cat='Integer' or equivalent) so the model respects integrality, especially when the objective is to minimize or maximize the number of units.

nodes.name: InfeasibilityMisinterpreted
nodes.text: Assuming a modeling mistake when the solver reports infeasibility, even though the constraints and objective correctly reflect an impossible set of requirements, capacities, and composition limits.

nodes.name: InfeasibilityMisinterpreted fix
nodes.text: Check logical feasibility of the narrative constraints (e.g., minimum production vs resource and proportion limits). If no integer solution satisfies all, document the problem as infeasible and keep the model; do not relax or remove constraints arbitrarily.

nodes.name: Two-channel minimum-cost requirement description
nodes.text: A compact MAMO Easy problem with two decision variables, usually channels/projects/options X and Y, minimizing total cost while meeting one or more requirement constraints.

nodes.name: Two-channel minimum-cost requirement model
nodes.text: Use x and y for the actual quantity/allocation/effectiveness/budget units chosen, not both quantity and spend unless the prompt explicitly distinguishes them. Minimize c_x*x + c_y*y when c_x and c_y are per-unit costs. Critical MAMO Easy convention: if the text says total budget/resource/allocation for X and Y combined cannot exceed B, model x + y <= B even when B is written with a dollar sign. Do not convert that combined allocation cap into c_x*x + c_y*y <= B merely because per-unit costs appear later. Use a cost/spending cap only when the prompt explicitly says total spending, total cost, or total expenditure cannot exceed B. Requirement/effectiveness constraints use >=; capacity/budget/maximum constraints use <=. Add integer domains only when the prompt says whole numbers, indivisible units, or integer budgets.

nodes.name: Two-channel minimum-cost requirement code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVar(lb=0,vtype=GRB.INTEGER); y=model.addVar(lb=0,vtype=GRB.INTEGER); model.setObjective(cx*x+cy*y, GRB.MINIMIZE); model.addConstr(ax*x+ay*y >= demand)

nodes.name: SpendQuantityConfusion
nodes.text: Confusing allocation/budget units with spending dollars. In MAMO Easy, phrases such as total budget/allocation/resource for X and Y combined cannot exceed B usually mean x + y <= B, even if B has a dollar sign; per-unit costs belong in the objective c_x*x + c_y*y unless the cap explicitly says total cost/spending/expenditure.

nodes.name: SpendQuantityConfusion fix
nodes.text: First decide what x and y count. If costs are per unit, x and y are units and total spend is cost_x*x + cost_y*y. If the prompt directly says allocate dollars, do not multiply those dollar variables by another cost coefficient.

nodes.name: RequirementDirection
nodes.text: A minimum reach/effectiveness/production requirement is modeled with <= instead of >=.

nodes.name: RequirementDirection fix
nodes.text: Translate must yield at least, minimum, required, no less than into >=.

nodes.name: FalseExactBudget
nodes.text: Forcing the budget/allocation cap to equality or replacing x + y <= B by c_x*x + c_y*y <= B. The optimum may use far less than the maximum allocation, and the cap unit must match the benchmark wording.

nodes.name: FalseExactBudget fix
nodes.text: Use <= for cannot exceed, at most, maximum. Use equality only for exactly or must use all.

nodes.name: MAMO Easy Ratio and Difference Constraints
Linearized ratio, multiple, and difference wording
nodes.problem_type: MAMO Easy Ratio and Difference Constraints

nodes.name: Linearized ratio, multiple, and difference wording description
nodes.text: MAMO Easy often encodes the key constraint in English with phrases like difference of at least, should exceed, no more than, twice, three times, or percentage share.

nodes.name: Linearized ratio, multiple, and difference wording model
nodes.text: Convert every ratio or difference phrase into a linear inequality before coding. For X exceeds Y by at least d, use x - y >= d. For X should not exceed twice Y by more than d, use x - 2*y <= d. For effort from X is three times greater than twice effort from Y with difference at least d, use 3*x - 2*y >= d if that is the stated score expression. Avoid variable division.

nodes.name: Linearized ratio, multiple, and difference wording code skeleton
nodes.snippet: model.addConstr(x - y >= d); model.addConstr(x - 2*y <= cap); model.addConstr(3*x - 2*y >= threshold)

nodes.name: RatioDirectionReversal
nodes.text: At least/at most ratio constraints are reversed.

nodes.name: RatioDirectionReversal fix
nodes.text: Write the English phrase as an algebra sentence before simplifying: X at least k times Y means x >= k*y; X no more than k times Y means x <= k*y.

nodes.name: DifferenceExpressionDropped
nodes.text: The threshold on a difference expression is omitted, making the optimum too cheap.

nodes.name: DifferenceExpressionDropped fix
nodes.text: Preserve the full left-hand expression and compare it to the stated threshold.

nodes.name: NonlinearRatio
nodes.text: The implementation divides by a decision variable.

nodes.name: NonlinearRatio fix
nodes.text: Cross multiply constants and keep all constraints linear.

nodes.name: Positive-cost lower-bound optimum description
nodes.text: A simple MAMO Easy minimization where each category has minimum required quantities and positive unit costs, sometimes with a total maximum capacity.

nodes.name: Positive-cost lower-bound optimum model
nodes.text: If all costs are positive and constraints are only lower bounds plus an upper capacity that is not binding at the minimum, the optimum is often exactly the minimum required quantities. Still build/solve the ILP, but use this as a sanity check.

nodes.name: Positive-cost lower-bound optimum code skeleton
nodes.snippet: x=model.addVar(lb=min_x,vtype=GRB.INTEGER); y=model.addVar(lb=min_y,vtype=GRB.INTEGER); z=model.addVar(lb=min_z,vtype=GRB.INTEGER); model.addConstr(x+y+z <= cap); model.setObjective(cx*x+cy*y+cz*z, GRB.MINIMIZE)

nodes.name: UnneededExtraQuantity
nodes.text: The model adds extra units even though every unit has positive cost and no constraint requires extras.

nodes.name: UnneededExtraQuantity fix
nodes.text: Check whether the lower-bound vector already satisfies all <= capacity constraints; if so it is optimal.

nodes.name: MinimumAsMaximum
nodes.text: Minimum required quantities are encoded as upper bounds.

nodes.name: MinimumAsMaximum fix
nodes.text: Use x >= minimum, not x <= minimum.

nodes.name: CapacityAsDemand
nodes.text: A total maximum is treated as a total demand equality.

nodes.name: CapacityAsDemand fix
nodes.text: Use x+y+z <= cap for cannot exceed.

nodes.name: Cost, effectiveness, and objective-unit sanity check
keywords: what would be the minimum total cost

nodes.name: Cost, effectiveness, and objective-unit sanity check description
nodes.text: A validation pattern for short MAMO Easy problems where a plausible but wrong model returns a number in the wrong unit or an implausible scale.

nodes.name: Cost, effectiveness, and objective-unit sanity check model
nodes.text: After solving, verify that the printed objective has the unit requested in the final question. If the answer asks dollars, output total dollars c_x*x + c_y*y. If it asks allocation units/effectiveness, output that quantity. Check scale carefully: a constraint like x + y <= B is in allocation/budget units in MAMO Easy, while c_x*x + c_y*y is in dollars/cost. Do not use a dollar objective as a budget cap unless the statement explicitly says total cost/spending/expenditure is capped.

nodes.name: Cost, effectiveness, and objective-unit sanity check code skeleton
nodes.snippet: assert obj_val is not None; print("Objective Value:", round(obj_val))

nodes.name: WrongOutputUnit
nodes.text: The solver prints x, y, effectiveness, or model status instead of the requested objective value.

nodes.name: WrongOutputUnit fix
nodes.text: Always print the objective value in the unit requested by the final question.

nodes.name: ScaleMismatch
nodes.text: The answer is off by a cost coefficient or 1000 multiplier.

nodes.name: ScaleMismatch fix
nodes.text: Check whether coefficients are dollars per unit, thousands of dollars, or raw units before output.

nodes.name: StatusAsAnswer
nodes.text: A solver status code is used as the prediction.

nodes.name: StatusAsAnswer fix
nodes.text: Only output a numeric objective when status is optimal; otherwise repair the model.

nodes.name: MAMO Easy monetary scale and reporting units

nodes.text: MAMO Easy often mixes dollars, thousands of dollars, budget units, and fee rates. Choose one reporting unit before modeling and output exactly the requested unit.

If the final question says in thousands, output objective/1000. If costs are stated as N thousand dollars and the question asks nearest thousand dollars, keep the objective in thousand-dollar units instead of multiplying by 1000. If large investment constraints use $100,000/$10,000 and coefficients are $5000/$4000 per normalized unit, use thousand-dollar decision units such as x=10 for $10,000. If coefficients are rates like 0.05 or 0.08, keep dollar variables and multiply by the rate.

nodes.name: ThousandScaleMismatch
nodes.text: Returning 1000 times the expected value by treating thousand-dollar coefficients as dollars, or by multiplying a value already expressed in thousands by 1000.
Normalize all monetary quantities to dollars or thousands before solving, then convert the final objective to the unit requested by the final sentence.

nodes.name: MAMO Easy objective value not allocation quantity

nodes.text: Many MAMO Easy problems ask for the minimum total cost after allocating resources. The requested answer is the evaluated objective, not the amount allocated.

For decision variables x_i and cost coefficients c_i, minimize and print sum_i c_i*x_i. Do not print sum_i x_i, a binding requirement value, or one decision variable when the final question asks for minimum total cost/expenditure.

nodes.name: AllocationInsteadOfObjective
nodes.text: The model solves correctly but outputs total allocation or a decision variable instead of the total cost objective.
After solving, compute obj = sum(c_i * value(x_i)) in the requested reporting unit and print result: obj.

MAMO Easy prompts often contain both requirement coefficients and objective coefficients. Build a ledger separating decision variable units, requirement coefficients, objective cost or score coefficients, RHS values, and requested reporting units. MAMO Easy benchmark convention: even if prose says cost per unit of effectiveness, when effectiveness is separately a*x+b*y and X/Y are the allocation variables, use cost_X*x + cost_Y*y, not cost_X*a*x + cost_Y*b*y.

Let x_i be the quantities in the unit named by the constraints. Requirement clauses create linear constraints. If the final target is minimum total cost or score, use objective min sum_i c_i*x_i where c_i comes from per-unit cost, fatigue score, staffing cost, production cost, or contribution-to-score phrases. Requirement/effectiveness coefficients such as 3*x+4*y>=R stay in constraints. If cost coefficients are 200 and 150 for X and Y, use 200*x+150*y; do not multiply by 3 and 4 again unless the prompt explicitly prices generated effectiveness. MAMO Easy benchmark convention: even if prose says cost per unit of effectiveness, when effectiveness is separately a*x+b*y and X/Y are the allocation variables, use cost_X*x + cost_Y*y, not cost_X*a*x + cost_Y*b*y.

nodes.snippet: Build a coefficient ledger from the original prompt; solve the LP/MILP; recompute audited_obj = sum(c[i] * value(x[i]) for i in items); print result: audited_obj.

nodes.name: ObjectiveCoefficientOmitted
nodes.text: The model solves a feasible allocation but prints x+y, a single variable, an RHS, or an effectiveness quantity instead of multiplying by the stated objective coefficients. A second error is double-counting requirement coefficients, e.g. using 200*3*x + 150*4*y when the correct cost objective is 200*x + 150*y. Double-counting effectiveness coefficients is wrong for MAMO Easy direct-cost convention.

Before accepting the answer, recompute the requested objective from solved variable values and all per-unit objective coefficients in the original text. Reject x+y unless all objective coefficients are 1.  Keep a separate requirement ledger and cost ledger: requirement coefficients build constraints; cost coefficients build the objective directly. MAMO Easy benchmark convention: even if prose says cost per unit of effectiveness, when effectiveness is separately a*x+b*y and X/Y are the allocation variables, use cost_X*x + cost_Y*y, not cost_X*a*x + cost_Y*b*y.

MAMO Easy wording frequently gives one-sided difference limits such as the difference between X and twice Y cannot exceed a bound. These are not absolute-value constraints unless absolute difference is explicitly stated.

Translate difference between A and twice B cannot exceed L as A - 2*B <= L. Translate A should be at least k more than B as A - B >= k. Use abs(A-B) only when the text explicitly says absolute difference.

nodes.snippet: Build a coefficient ledger from the original prompt; solve the LP/MILP; recompute audited_obj = sum(c[i] * value(x[i]) for i in items); print result: audited_obj.

nodes.name: WrongDifferenceDirection
nodes.text: A one-sided difference limit is reversed, treated as an absolute difference, or attached to the wrong variables.
Write the inequality exactly in the order stated by the sentence, then check it against a simple feasible example before solving.

Many MAMO Easy instances have two to four integer variables and modest bounds. A small enumeration or objective recomputation can catch wrong objectives and wrong inequality directions before accepting the answer.

For small integer LPs, solve with PuLP and, when bounds are modest, optionally enumerate feasible integer assignments to confirm the best objective. Always recompute the final target from variable values.

nodes.snippet: Build a coefficient ledger from the original prompt; solve the LP/MILP; recompute audited_obj = sum(c[i] * value(x[i]) for i in items); print result: audited_obj.

nodes.name: UncheckedSmallIntegerResult
nodes.text: The solver result is accepted even though a simple enumeration or recomputation would reveal a missing objective coefficient, wrong difference direction, or infeasible interpretation.

Use the original text to recompute the target scalar from the returned variables. For modest integer ranges, compare against a brute-force feasible search or at least verify all constraints and the objective ledger.

nodes.name: Production capacity and resource trade-off description
nodes.text: The problem asks how many products or activities to produce under limited machine time, labor, material, budget, or capacity, with profit or cost coefficients driving the objective.

nodes.name: Multi-period inventory balance description
nodes.text: The prompt contains periods, inventory carryover, production levels, hiring, firing, outsourcing, or holding costs, requiring balance equations that link decisions across time.

nodes.name: Shift staffing coverage description
nodes.text: The problem assigns workers, nurses, employees, or shifts to cover time-period demand while minimizing staffing cost or meeting coverage requirements.

nodes.name: Blending requirement description
nodes.text: The problem mixes ingredients, foods, feeds, materials, or sources to satisfy lower and upper bounds on nutrients, quality, composition, or demand at minimum cost.

nodes.name: Transportation supply-demand description
nodes.text: The problem ships flow from origins to destinations with supply and demand constraints, usually minimizing transportation cost over route-specific unit costs.

nodes.name: Network flow balance description
nodes.text: The prompt describes nodes, arcs, sources, sinks, capacities, costs, or paths, requiring conservation or shortest-path style constraints on a network.

nodes.name: Routing and tour selection description
nodes.text: The problem involves visiting customers, cities, locations, or delivery points with vehicles or tours, often requiring route selection, assignment, and travel-cost minimization.

nodes.name: Assignment and matching description
nodes.text: The problem assigns jobs, tasks, people, machines, or resources to one another with one-to-one or capacity-limited matching constraints.

nodes.name: Facility location decision description
nodes.text: The problem chooses which facilities, warehouses, centers, or service sites to open and how to assign customers or demand points to opened locations.

nodes.name: Coverage model description
nodes.text: The prompt asks to cover areas, customers, demand points, skills, services, or requirements using a subset of candidate facilities, routes, or resources.

nodes.name: Selection under budget description
nodes.text: The problem selects projects, items, assets, investments, or options under budget, risk, weight, or resource limits to maximize value or return.

nodes.name: Price-demand nonlinear description
nodes.text: The prompt includes price, demand, revenue, profit, or quadratic relationships, requiring nonlinear or linearized reasoning over price-dependent demand.

nodes.name: Binary logic modeling description
nodes.text: The problem requires integer or binary variables to encode yes-or-no choices, activation decisions, logical implications, mutually exclusive options, or fixed-charge behavior.
